description: Proyek teknologi yang mengubah data terbuka NASA tentang luar angkasa dan Bumi menjadi pengalaman interaktif dan mudah dipahami, sehingga pengguna dapat mengeksplorasi informasi sains dengan cara yang menarik.
summary: We developed Crorb, a web-based agricultural decision support dashboard that helps farmers and field managers assess land suitability using real environmental data. The platform combines satellite NDVI imagery, weather and climate data, soil conditions, and terrain information to analyze a selected field location and generate crop recommendations. It addresses the challenge of making data-driven farming decisions when growers often rely on fragmented or incomplete information. By integrating multiple reliable sources into a single interface, Crorb makes it easier to evaluate field conditions, and choose suitable crops based on location-specific evidence. This is important because better crop planning can improve productivity, reduce risk, and support more sustainable farming practices in the face of climate variability and limited agricultural insight.
details:
Project overview

Crorb is a web app that helps farmers understand field conditions and explore crops suited to a selected location. Users draw a field boundary on a satellite map, Crorb uses the area’s midpoint to gather and display relevant information.

The app brings together historical climate data from NASA POWER, soil properties from SoilGrids, weather forecasts from Meteomatics, terrain data such as elevation and slope, and Sentinel-2 imagery with NDVI indicators. It presents these results across field overview, weather and climate, and soil conditions pages. and it also provide crop recommendations and explanations based on the collected data using ai.

Benefits and intended impact

Crorb makes several kinds of environmental data easier to review in one place, helping users compare field conditions and make more informed growing decisions. Its intended impact is to support practical, data-informed crop planning—while serving as a decision aid rather than a replacement for local expertise or professional agricultural advice.

Tools and technologies

The project uses Python for the web server and data integration, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend. It uses Leaflet for the interactive map, connects to external climate, soil, satellite, and forecasting data sources, and uses OpenRouter ai model for crop recommendations. It is designed to run as a web service on Railway. No specialized hardware is required beyond a computer and an internet connection.

Creative approach and factors considered

Crorb creative element is combining diverse datasets from satellite imagery to soil and weather measurements in a single interactive field focused experience. The design also considers field boundary size and coordinate accuracy, the availability of external data providers.

Disadvantages / Limitations

  • Crop Recommendation Accuracy: The crop recommendations are generated by an AI model that has not been sufficiently fine-tuned or trained on a comprehensive crop dataset. As a result, its recommendations may not always be accurate or optimal for real-world agricultural conditions.
  • Limited Dataset Availability: We also explored implementing a rule-based scoring system, but encountered difficulties due to the lack of sufficient data and the absence of a complete, reliable, and publicly available open-source agricultural dataset.
  • Slow Data Analyze: The data analysis process can take a considerable amount of time, especially when retrieving and processing data from multiple sources, such as NASA POWER, Microsoft Planetary Computer, and SoilGrids. Some operations involving satellite imagery and geospatial data processing are particularly time-consuming.
  • Frontend Code Quality: The frontend was developed with assistance from GitHub Copilot. While this helped speed up development, some parts of the code may be messy, inconsistent, or require further refactoring and optimization.
